structured.answer: If I go with the page's default (Interactive Israel plus the iShares Core S&P 500 Accumulating fund), the 70,000 ₪ I'd put in over 10 years comes to about 84,184 ₪ after costs, and the page's "הזוג הזול ביותר" comes to 86,492 ₪. But I couldn't work out which account and fund that cheapest pair is, and I'd never heard of Interactive Israel, so I didn't open anything today.

stuck.where: Top result card, 'הזוג הזול ביותר לתוכנית שלכם' 86,492 ₪
stuck.why: It's the number the page seems to recommend, but the card doesn't say which bank or fund it is. All it gives me is a 'בחרו את הזוג הזה' link.

stuck.where: Accounts list, first place 'אינטראקטיב ישראל (מותק של MEXEM LTD)'
stuck.why: It's ranked cheapest, but I've never heard the name. The banks I know (לאומי 71,513, מזרחי 69,201) leave me with way less.

stuck.where: Fund list on the left, 'בלי נטרול מט"ח · 19 קרנות'
stuck.why: Too many funds that look the same, all covered in little coloured tags. Some show minus numbers like '−533 ₪' and '−2.44%', which scared me off.
The page starts at 10,000 ₪ today, not my 30,000. In screenshots I can't change it, so every number is for 10,000 plus 500 a month.

findings.what: The 'הזוג הזול ביותר' card gives a number (86,492) but no name for the account and fund in that pair
The cheapest place is a name I've never heard (MEXEM LTD), and the big banks come out much lower
Way too many funds that look alike, with lots of tags I don't understand
Minus numbers and red tags next to funds made me scared to pick any of them
Costs in shekels (1,298 vs 15,351) are what actually landed for me. The percents meant nothing
